newsitem.title: JAPAN: US-Japan trade ties entering 'delicate' period--US.
newsitem.headline: US-Japan trade ties entering 'delicate' period--US.

text.p: The United States feels that U.S.-Japan trade relations are entering "a rather delicate and potentially difficult" period, a U.S. official told reporters on Tuesday.
"In our view, we are entering a rather delicate and potentially difficult period in U.S.-Japan trade relations," the official said.
"For the past three years there was a steady improvement in Japan's external accounts...and Japan's bilateral surplus with the United States has also fallen," he said.

"Now that progress appears to be reversing, stalling a bit...I'm not saying with certainty we are going to see a large increase in the current account surplus this year, but we are worried about these signs," he said.

He added that the United States was concerned that a "combination of external factors and severe contraction in fiscal policy" would prematurely end Japan's economic recovery and lead to an increase in its surplus.

The official said these factors were creating an environment in which it was very easy for trade disputes to develop and intensify. "It's like a drought in a forest. It doesn't take much of a spark to create a fire," he said.

He said the U.S. trade agenda with Japan will focus on three elements of implementing and monitoring existing agreements, World Trade Organisation obligations and an increased emphasis on Japanese deregulation.
